title: Faux Polyglot: A Study on Information Disparity in Multilingual Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multilingual LLMs in a cross-language Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using a synthetic fictional dataset with conflicting facts across five languages. The study measures retrieval preference using normalized cosine similarity scores and generation preference using Information Overlap (BERTScore and keyword matching) to identify systemic bias toward documents in the query's native language.

Measuring the 'second language preference' in both retrieval and generation phases when documents in the query's native language are absent. The study calculates the rate at which models default to retrieving or generating answers from high-resource languages (e.g., English, German) versus lower-resource languages (e.g., Arabic, Hindi).
